_comment: Frozen retrieval cases. Every expectation here was checked against the
corpora actually in the repo -- the three lore pages in data/raw/lore.json
and the Episode IV dialogue file from the star-wars-scripts submodule --
so a failure means retrieval changed, not that the case was aspirational.
corpus: 'lore' cases need data/raw/lore.json to still contain that page.
The scraper is rate-limited by Fandom and the current lore.json holds only
3 of the 8 pages it requests, so scripts/run_retrieval_eval.py reports
these separately instead of scoring a missing page as a retrieval miss.
Add a case whenever a retrieval bug is fixed. That is the whole point: the
suite grows into a record of what this system has gotten wrong before.

cases.query: What is the Code of the Sith?
cases.note: The canonical lore lookup. If this misses, the lore half of the index is broken.

cases.query: Through passion I gain strength, through strength power
cases.note: Near-verbatim query. Dense retrieval should find this trivially; if it does not, embeddings are misconfigured.

cases.query: Who established the Rule of Two and why only two Sith?
cases.note: Proper noun in the expectation -- exactly where dense-only retrieval is weakest and BM25 would help.

cases.query: Must the Sith apprentice kill their master?
cases.note: The answer lives in a later chunk of the article than the Bane sentence, so this and the case above should hit different chunks.

cases.query: How many forms of communication is the protocol droid fluent in?
cases.note: Non-Sith lore. Guards against a retriever that has quietly become a Sith-only index.

cases.query: Vader threatening an officer who doubts the Force
cases.note: The most-quoted line in the corpus, and the case that proves the persona speaker filter resolves VADER.

cases.query: Vader demanding to know where the stolen plans were sent
cases.note: Several Vader lines satisfy this; the case asserts the filter returns his voice, not which line.

cases.query: Vader sensing a powerful presence in the Force
cases.note: Short line, ~34 characters. Short chunks embed poorly next to 500-character lore chunks; a miss here is a chunking problem, not a query problem.

cases.query: What does the dark side promise its followers?
cases.note: The one case that grades the lore/dialogue rebalance itself: it expects both halves back in a single k=4 result set, which only holds if lore_weight is doing its job.

cases.query: the Rebel Alliance and the Death Star plans
cases.note: A query whose best dialogue matches are mostly spoken by Leia, Han and Tarkin. Asserts the persona filter still surfaces a Vader line rather than falling back to whoever ranked highest.
